title: Greedy Best-First in Reykjavík: find the quickest way!
description: Watch Greedy Best-First race across a real street-grid graph to reach a target with lightning-fast decision-making. The visualization highlights how the algorithm prioritizes nodes by heuristic distance instead of path cost.
ig_caption:
❄️🚗 Reykjavík streets turned into a graph! In this visualization, **Greedy Best-First** explores intersections by always choosing the next node with the **smallest heuristic estimate** to the goal (typically *h(n)* = straight-line or travel-time proxy), not the lowest total cost so far.

🧠 In graph-search terms: it uses a priority queue ordered by **h(n)**, making it *fast* and goal-directed—but not guaranteed optimal. On real street maps, each road segment becomes an edge with weights, while intersections become vertices; the heuristic effectively guides the search like a GPS “as-the-crow-flies” distance.

📍 Can you spot where the heuristic misleads it into detours? Drop a 🧭 in the comments if you want an A* comparison next! 

🎥 Follow for more real-map pathfinding visuals + algorithm breakdowns.
fb_caption:
🚦 Reykjavík (Vesturbær) + **Greedy Best-First**! This reel shows how a graph search works: intersections are vertices, roads are edges, and the algorithm picks the next stop using only the heuristic distance to the goal.

⚡ It’s quick because it’s guided by *where the target seems to be*, but it may skip the globally shortest route. If you enjoyed the visualization, share it with a friend learning algorithms or tag someone who loves coding!
yt_description:
Greedy Best-First pathfinding visualization in Reykjavík (Vesturbær)! Watch a priority-queue graph search choose the next intersection using only a heuristic distance to the goal. Learn how real street maps become graphs (nodes=intersections, edges=roads) and why Greedy Best-First is fast but not always optimal.

Keywords: greedy best first, pathfinding visualization, graph search, heuristic, priority queue, algorithms, computerscience, street map graph, A* vs Greedy.
